third_party_evaluations.summary: CSA cloud-native security guidance frequently cites CKS as a baseline credential for Kubernetes cluster security engineers.

evaluation.rationale: Independent reviews of the stored evidence produced specialty: 3. The existing unordered-specialty rule applies when at least one reviewer identifies a specialty track. See each persona rationale for the supporting factors and limitations.

hiroshi-tanaka.rationale: The required CKA and live-cluster security tasks establish a focused Kubernetes security specialization, consistent with the recorded specialty hint; frequent version changes limit longevity without ongoing practice.

maria-okonkwo.rationale: The prior CKA requirement and live cluster security tasks establish a focused Kubernetes security specialization. This practical signal is valuable for cloud-native staffing, while version churn and platform concentration make a general seniority ranking misleading.

alex-novak.rationale: The live-cluster security practical and required prior CKA make this a substantive extension to an existing Kubernetes track. Its focused cluster-security scope fits unordered specialty better than a general seniority rank.
